AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. Consider enabling the autogrowth setting for all data and log files on your target SQL Server instance after the migration is completed.

 
While you still set autogrowth ON, for a managed production system, you must consider autogrowth to be merely a contingency for unexpected growth. Do not manage your data and log growth on a day-to-day basis with autogrowth.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: Verify autogrowth is turned on for all data and log files during the upgrade process. (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798526)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: ORDER BY specifies integer ordinal
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: This rule checks stored procedures, functions, views and triggers for use of ORDER BY clause specifying ordinal column numbers as sort columns. A sort column can be specified as a nonnegative integer representing the position of the name or alias in the select list, but this is not recommended. An integer cannot be specified when the order_by_expression appears in a ranking function. A sort column can include an expression, but when the database is in SQL 90 compatibility mode or higher, the expression cannot resolve to a constant.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation: Specify the sort column as a name or column alias rather than hard coding the ordinal.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
Bad habits to kick : ORDER BY ordinal (https://aka.ms/order-by-integer) 
DISCLAIMER: Third-party link provided as-is and Microsoft does not offer any guarantees or warranties regarding the content on the third party site.

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. Consider enabling the autogrowth setting for all data and log files on your target SQL Server instance after the migration is completed.

 
While you still set autogrowth ON, for a managed production system, you must consider autogrowth to be merely a contingency for unexpected growth. Do not manage your data and log growth on a day-to-day basis with autogrowth.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: Verify autogrowth is turned on for all data and log files during the upgrade process. (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798526)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. Consider enabling the autogrowth setting for all data and log files on your target SQL Server instance after the migration is completed.

 
While you still set autogrowth ON, for a managed production system, you must consider autogrowth to be merely a contingency for unexpected growth. Do not manage your data and log growth on a day-to-day basis with autogrowth.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: Verify autogrowth is turned on for all data and log files during the upgrade process. (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798526)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. Consider enabling the autogrowth setting for all data and log files on your target SQL Server instance after the migration is completed.

 
While you still set autogrowth ON, for a managed production system, you must consider autogrowth to be merely a contingency for unexpected growth. Do not manage your data and log growth on a day-to-day basis with autogrowth.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: Verify autogrowth is turned on for all data and log files during the upgrade process. (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798526)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. Consider enabling the autogrowth setting for all data and log files on your target SQL Server instance after the migration is completed.

 
While you still set autogrowth ON, for a managed production system, you must consider autogrowth to be merely a contingency for unexpected growth. Do not manage your data and log growth on a day-to-day basis with autogrowth.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: Verify autogrowth is turned on for all data and log files during the upgrade process. (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798526)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. Consider enabling the autogrowth setting for all data and log files on your target SQL Server instance after the migration is completed.

 
While you still set autogrowth ON, for a managed production system, you must consider autogrowth to be merely a contingency for unexpected growth. Do not manage your data and log growth on a day-to-day basis with autogrowth.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: Verify autogrowth is turned on for all data and log files during the upgrade process. (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798526)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: ORDER BY specifies integer ordinal
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: This rule checks stored procedures, functions, views and triggers for use of ORDER BY clause specifying ordinal column numbers as sort columns. A sort column can be specified as a nonnegative integer representing the position of the name or alias in the select list, but this is not recommended. An integer cannot be specified when the order_by_expression appears in a ranking function. A sort column can include an expression, but when the database is in SQL 90 compatibility mode or higher, the expression cannot resolve to a constant.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation: Specify the sort column as a name or column alias rather than hard coding the ordinal.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
Bad habits to kick : ORDER BY ordinal (https://aka.ms/order-by-integer)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Turn on autogrowth for all data and log files after the migration is completed on the target server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: You may experience transaction failures when database data or log files run out of space.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Assessment detected data or log files on your source SQL Server that do not have autogrowth enabled. New and enhanced features require additional disk space for user databases and the tempdb system database. Consider enabling the autogrowth setting for all data and log files on your target SQL Server instance after the migration is completed.

 
While you still set autogrowth ON, for a managed production system, you must consider autogrowth to be merely a contingency for unexpected growth. Do not manage your data and log growth on a day-to-day basis with autogrowth.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: Verify autogrowth is turned on for all data and log files during the upgrade process. (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798526)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: FOR XML AUTO queries return derived table references in 90 or later compatibility modes
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: When the database compatibility level is set to 90 or later, FOR XML queries that execute in AUTO mode return references to derived table aliases. When the compatibility level is set to 80, FOR XML AUTO queries return references to the base tables that define a derived table. For example, the following query, which includes a derived table, produces different results under compatibility levels 80, 90, or later: SELECT * FROM (SELECT a.id AS a, b.id AS b FROM Test a JOIN Test b ON a.id=b.id) AS DerivedTest FOR XML AUTO; Under compatibility level 80, the query returns the following results. The results reference the base table aliases a and b of the derived table instead of the derived table alias. Under compatibility level 90 or later, the query returns references to the derived table alias DerivedTest instead of to the derived table's base tables.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation: Modify your application as required to account for the changes in results of FOR XML AUTO queries that include derived tables and that run under compatibility level 90 or later.

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: Unqualified Join(s) detected
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: Starting with database compatibility level 90 and higher, in rare occasions, the 'unqualified join' syntax can cause 'missing join predicate' warnings, leading to long running queries.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
An example of "Unqualified join" is
 
select * from table1, table2
where table1.col1 = table2.col1

 Use  explicit JOIN syntax in all cases. SQL Server supports the below explicit joins:
 - LEFT OUTER JOIN or LEFT JOIN
- RIGHT OUTER JOIN or RIGHT JOIN
- FULL OUTER JOIN or FULL JOIN
- INNER JOIN
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
- Missing join Predicate Event Class (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798567)
- Deprecation of "Old Style" JOIN Syntax: Only A Partial Thing (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798568)
- DOC : Please strive to use ANSI-style joins instead of deprecated syntax  (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798569)
- Missing join predicate icon should be red (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798570)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: ORDER BY specifies integer ordinal
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: This rule checks stored procedures, functions, views and triggers for use of ORDER BY clause specifying ordinal column numbers as sort columns. A sort column can be specified as a nonnegative integer representing the position of the name or alias in the select list, but this is not recommended. An integer cannot be specified when the order_by_expression appears in a ranking function. A sort column can include an expression, but when the database is in SQL 90 compatibility mode or higher, the expression cannot resolve to a constant.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation: Specify the sort column as a name or column alias rather than hard coding the ordinal.
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo:
Bad habits to kick : ORDER BY ordinal (https://aka.ms/order-by-integer)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: SQL Mail has been discontinued
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact:
SQL Mail has been discontinued starting from SQL Server 2012. 
 SQL Mail runs in-process to SQL Server service. If SQL Mail goes down, so does the server. Database Mail runs outside SQL Server in a separate process, is scalable, and does not require Extended MAPI client components to be installed on the production server.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
Avoid using this feature in new development work, and plan to modify applications that currently use this feature. To send mail, use Database Mail.
 Use Database Mail instead of SQL Mail (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798566)
AssessmentRecommendations.MoreInfo: SQL Mail (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=798565)

AssessmentRecommendations.Title: CLR assemblies marked as SAFE or EXTERNAL_ACCESS are considered UNSAFE
AssessmentRecommendations.Impact: CLR Strict Security mode is introduced in SQL Server 2017. This mode is enabled by default and introduces breaking changes for databases containing user-defined CLR assemblies marked either SAFE or EXTERNAL_ACCESS.
AssessmentRecommendations.Recommendation:
When CLR Strict Security is enabled, attempting to create an unsigned assembly will cause an error. Use the following steps to create a signed assembly:

  1. Create a key pair file. For more information, see How to: Create a Public-Private Key Pair.
  2. Compile the module and sign it using the key file. For more information, see How to: Sign an Assembly with a Strong Name.
  3. Create an asymmetric key in the master database from the key file CREATE ASYMMETRIC KEY MyStrongNameKey FROM FILE = 'C:\MyStrongNameKey.snk'
  4. Create a login from the asymmetric key CREATE LOGIN MyStrongNameKeyLogin FROM ASYMMETRIC KEY MyStrongNameKey
  5. Grant UNSAFE ASSEMBLY permission to the login GRANT UNSAFE ASSEMBLY TO MyStrongNameKeyLogin
  6. Now users with CREATE ASSEMBLY permissions can create assemblies signed by the key
We recommend signing assemblies by following the steps outlined above. However, you can alternatively do one of the following:
  • Set the Trustworthy Property of the database to ON and grant UNSAFE ASSEMBLY permission to the login that owns the database. This is not recommended because marking a database as Trustworthy can allow malicious assemblies to impact resources outside the database. For more information, see Guidelines for using the TRUSTWORTHY database setting in SQL Server.
  • Disable CLR Strict Security by using sp_configure. This is not recommended because assemblies marked SAFE or EXTERNAL_ACCESS may enable elevation of privilege from a database user to a sysadmin. sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1 GO sp_configure 'clr strict security', 0 GO RECONFIGURE GO
